description: These iconic Hong Kong Pineapple Buns, or Bo Lo Bao, feature a wonderfully soft, sweet bread crowned with a delicate, crispy, crumbly topping that resembles a pineapple's skin. Despite their name, there's no actual pineapple in them; the name comes purely from their distinctive appearance. Perfect for breakfast or a delightful snack, these buns offer a delightful contrast of textures and flavors.

instructions.title: Prepare the Bun Dough
instructions.text: In a large mixing bowl, combine bread flour, 40g granulated sugar, instant yeast, and salt. Add the whole egg and warm milk. Mix with a spatula or stand mixer on low speed until a shaggy dough forms. Knead for about 5-7 minutes until the dough comes together. Add the softened 30g unsalted butter and continue kneading for another 8-10 minutes until the dough is smooth, elastic, and passes the windowpane test. Place the dough in a lightly oiled bowl, cover with plastic wrap, and let it proof in a warm place for 60-90 minutes, or until doubled in size.

instructions.title: Make the Pineapple Topping
instructions.text: While the dough is proofing, prepare the topping. In a separate bowl, cream together the softened 60g unsalted butter and powdered sugar until light and fluffy. Beat in the egg yolk until well combined. Sift in the all-purpose flour and milk powder, then gently fold until just combined. Do not overmix. The mixture should be soft but pliable. Divide the topping into 8 equal portions and roll each into a ball. Set aside in the refrigerator to firm up slightly.

instructions.title: Shape the Buns
instructions.text: Once the dough has doubled, gently punch it down to release air. Transfer the dough to a lightly floured surface and divide it into 8 equal portions. Roll each portion into a smooth ball. Flatten each dough ball into a round disc. Take one portion of the chilled topping, flatten it into a disc slightly larger than your dough ball, and carefully place it over the dough ball. Gently press and smooth the topping over the bun, creating a dome shape, leaving the bottom exposed. Repeat for all buns.

instructions.title: Second Proofing
instructions.text: Arrange the shaped buns on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper, leaving enough space between them. Cover the baking sheet loosely with plastic wrap or a clean kitchen towel. Let the buns proof again in a warm place for another 30-45 minutes, or until visibly puffy and slightly increased in size. Towards the end of the proofing, preheat your oven to 180 degrees Celsius (350 degrees Fahrenheit).

instructions.title: Bake the Pineapple Buns
instructions.text: Before baking, gently brush the tops of the buns with the egg wash (1 egg yolk whisked with 1 teaspoon of milk). You can also use a knife to gently score a crisscross pattern on the topping for a more authentic pineapple-skin look, being careful not to cut into the dough. Bake in the preheated oven for 15-20 minutes, or until the topping is golden brown and crispy, and the buns are cooked through. The exact baking time may vary depending on your oven.

instructions.title: Cool and Serve
instructions.text: Once baked, remove the Pineapple Buns from the oven and transfer them to a wire rack to cool slightly. These buns are best enjoyed warm, ideally within a few hours of baking, when the topping is at its crispiest. Serve them plain or with a slice of cold butter inserted into the center for a traditional Hong Kong style treat.

tips: Do not overmix the topping dough; overworking it can make it tough. Mix until just combined.
For an extra rich flavor, you can substitute some of the milk in the bun dough with evaporated milk.
If your topping is too sticky to handle, chill it in the refrigerator for a bit longer. If it's too crumbly, add a tiny bit more egg yolk or milk.
article:
Craving a taste of Hong Kong's bustling bakeries without leaving your kitchen? Look no further than the iconic Pineapple Bun, or Bo Lo Bao. This beloved Chinese pastry, with its signature crumbly, sweet crust and soft, fluffy bread, is a comforting treat enjoyed by millions. While its name might suggest a tropical fruit filling, the "pineapple" refers solely to the bun's distinctive cracked, golden-brown topping, resembling the fruit's rough skin. Learning this classic Pineapple Bun Recipe allows you to recreate an authentic culinary experience right at home, filling your kitchen with an irresistible aroma that transports you to the vibrant streets of Asia.

## What is Pineapple Bun (Bo Lo Bao)?

Bo Lo Bao, or Pineapple Bun, is a staple in Hong Kong-style bakeries and dim sum restaurants worldwide. Despite its name, there's no actual pineapple in the bun itself. The moniker comes from the golden, sugar-crusted topping that cracks during baking, creating a pattern reminiscent of a pineapple's exterior. Beneath this delightfully sweet and slightly crispy crust lies a soft, airy, and slightly sweet yeast bread. It’s a masterclass in contrasting textures and flavors – the rich, buttery topping perfectly complements the tender bread beneath. Often enjoyed for breakfast or as an afternoon tea snack, it pairs wonderfully with a cup of milk tea or coffee. It's a simple pleasure that embodies the heart of Cantonese baking, a comfort food that evokes nostalgia for many and delight for all who try it.

## Ingredients for Homemade Pineapple Buns

Crafting the perfect Bo Lo Bao involves two main components: the soft bread dough and the iconic pineapple topping. Here's what you'll need for this delightful Pineapple Bun Recipe:

For the Bread Dough:
*   2 ½ cups (300g) all-purpose flour
*   ¼ cup (50g) granulated sugar
*   1 teaspoon active dry yeast
*   ¼ teaspoon salt
*   ½ cup (120ml) warm milk (around 105-115°F / 40-46°C)
*   1 large egg, lightly beaten
*   2 tablespoons (28g) unsalted butter, softened

For the Pineapple Topping:
*   ½ cup (113g) unsalted butter, softened
*   ½ cup (100g) granulated sugar
*   1 large egg yolk
*   1 large egg, lightly beaten (for egg wash)
*   1 ½ cups (180g) all-purpose flour
*   2 tablespoons milk powder (optional, but enhances flavor and texture)
*   ½ teaspoon baking powder

## Step-by-Step Instructions to Make Bo Lo Bao

Making Bo Lo Bao is a rewarding process that combines the art of bread making with pastry creation. Follow this comprehensive Pineapple Bun Recipe to bake your own batch of these irresistible treats:

1.  **Prepare the Bread Dough:**
    *   In a large bowl, whisk together the flour, sugar, yeast, and salt.
    *   In a separate bowl, combine the warm milk and beaten egg.
    *   Pour the wet ingredients into the dry ingredients. Mix with a spoon or your hands until a shaggy dough forms.
    *   Turn the dough out onto a lightly floured surface and knead for about 5-7 minutes until it becomes somewhat smooth.
    *   Add the softened butter and continue kneading for another 5-10 minutes until the butter is fully incorporated and the dough is smooth, elastic, and passes the windowpane test (you can stretch a small piece thin enough to see light through it without tearing).
    *   Place the dough in a lightly oiled bowl, cover with plastic wrap, and let it proof in a warm place for 1-1.5 hours, or until doubled in size.

2.  **Prepare the Pineapple Topping:**
    *   While the dough is proofing, make the topping. In a medium bowl, cream together the softened butter and sugar until light and fluffy.
    *   Beat in the egg yolk until well combined.
    *   In a separate bowl, whisk together the flour, milk powder (if using), and baking powder.
    *   Gradually add the dry ingredients to the wet ingredients, mixing until a soft dough forms. Do not overmix.
    *   Wrap the topping dough in plastic wrap and chill in the refrigerator for at least 30 minutes. This makes it easier to handle.

3.  **Assemble the Buns:**
    *   Once the bread dough has doubled, gently punch it down to release the air.
    *   Divide the dough into 8-10 equal pieces (about 60-70g each). Roll each piece into a smooth ball.
    *   Preheat your oven to 350°F (175°C). Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
    *   Remove the chilled topping dough from the refrigerator. Divide it into the same number of pieces as your bread dough.
    *   Take one piece of topping dough and flatten it into a thin disc, about 3-4 inches (7-10 cm) in diameter, using your palms or a rolling pin. The edges can be a little uneven, as this helps create the "pineapple" effect.
    *   Carefully place a topping disc over a bread dough ball, gently pressing it down and shaping it to cover about two-thirds to three-quarters of the bun's surface. Try to keep the topping off the very bottom of the bun so it can expand properly.
    *   Arrange the assembled buns on the prepared baking sheet, leaving some space between them.

4.  **Second Proofing and Baking:**
    *   Lightly brush the topping of each bun with the beaten egg (the one set aside for egg wash). Use a fork to gently score a crisscross pattern on the topping. This enhances the "pineapple" look and helps with cracking.
    *   Let the buns proof for a second time in a warm place for another 30-45 minutes, or until visibly puffy.
    *   Bake in the preheated oven for 15-20 minutes, or until the topping is golden brown and cracked, and the bread is cooked through.
    *   Remove from the oven and let cool slightly on a wire rack before serving.

## Tips for Perfect Pineapple Buns

Achieving bakery-quality Bo Lo Bao at home is entirely possible with a few key tips:

*   **Dough Consistency is Key:** Don't rush the kneading process. A well-kneaded dough will be smooth, elastic, and result in a wonderfully soft bun. If your dough is too sticky, add a tiny bit more flour; if too dry, a few drops of milk.
*   **Proofing Environment:** A warm, slightly humid environment is ideal for dough rising. You can create this by placing the covered dough in a turned-off oven with a bowl of hot water inside.
*   **Chilled Topping:** Ensure your pineapple topping dough is well-chilled. This makes it much easier to handle, roll, and place on the buns without it becoming too sticky or falling apart.
*   **Don't Over-Cover:** When applying the topping, aim to cover about 2/3 to 3/4 of the bun. Leaving some of the bread exposed at the bottom allows the bun to expand properly and prevents the topping from sliding off during baking.
*   **Egg Wash and Scoring:** The egg wash gives the topping that beautiful golden sheen, and the gentle scoring with a fork encourages the characteristic cracks, truly making it look like a pineapple.
*   **Freshness Matters:** While this Pineapple Bun Recipe yields delicious results, remember that homemade buns are best enjoyed fresh, ideally on the day they are baked, for the crispiest topping and softest bread.

## Serving Suggestions & Variations

Pineapple Buns are incredibly versatile and can be enjoyed in many ways beyond simply fresh from the oven.

*   **Classic "Bolo Yau":** The most famous variation involves slicing the warm bun horizontally and inserting a thick slab of cold butter. The warmth of the bun melts the butter slightly, creating a truly decadent experience known as "Bolo Yau" (butter pineapple bun).
*   **Breakfast Sandwich:** In Hong Kong cafes, Bo Lo Bao is often split and filled with savory items like scrambled eggs and luncheon meat, creating a unique and satisfying breakfast sandwich.
*   **Sweet Fillings:** While traditionally plain inside, you can easily adapt this Pineapple Bun Recipe by incorporating sweet fillings. Try adding a dollop of custard cream, red bean paste, or even a small square of chocolate inside the bread dough before its second proofing.
*   **Savory Fillings:** For a more adventurous twist, some bakeries offer Bo Lo Bao filled with savory char siu (BBQ pork) or even ham and cheese. This transforms the sweet bun into a delightful savory snack.
*   **With Beverages:** Pair your Bo Lo Bao with traditional Hong Kong milk tea, a strong cup of coffee, or simply a glass of cold milk for a comforting snack.

## Storage and Reheating Tips

Bo Lo Bao is undoubtedly at its best when enjoyed warm and fresh from the oven, with the topping still crispy and the bread soft. However, if you have leftovers, here's how to store and reheat them:

*   **Room Temperature:** Store leftover Pineapple Buns in an airtight container at room temperature for up to 1-2 days. The topping will lose some of its crispness over time, but the bread will remain soft.
*   **Freezing Baked Buns:** For longer storage, you can freeze baked Bo Lo Bao. Wrap each bun individually in plastic wrap, then place them in a freezer-safe bag or container. They can be frozen for up to 1 month.
*   **Freezing Dough:** You can also freeze the shaped bread dough balls (before the second proofing and adding topping) for later use. Thaw overnight in the refrigerator, then let them come to room temperature and proceed with the second proofing, topping application, and baking.
*   **Reheating:** To restore some of the bun's original glory, especially the crispiness of the topping, reheat them in a toaster oven or conventional oven. Preheat to 300°F (150°C) and bake for 5-10 minutes, or until warmed through and the topping feels slightly crisp again. Avoid microwaving, as it will make the topping soggy.

Embarking on this Pineapple Bun Recipe journey is a delightful way to explore the rich world of Chinese baking. From the satisfaction of kneading the perfect dough to the joy of seeing the signature cracks form on the golden topping, every step is a testament to the simple pleasures of homemade food. So gather your ingredients, follow these steps, and prepare to impress yourself and your loved ones with a batch of authentic, irresistible Bo Lo Bao.
